text:
rachel: decided to move my desk to the roof hatch today for 'fresh air + productivity'. also discovered hammocks make terrible monitor stands. :hammock:
diego: photos or it's a nap. :eyes:
matt: do you live on a pirate ship now? :pirate_flag:
rachel: https://imgur.com/a/roofnap - honestly vibe is immaculate but signal drops when the neighbor's tree sway. thinking about a DIY directional antenna. anyone tried a tinfoil parabolic reflector?
zara: haha yes to tiny pirate vibes. i built a cheap reflector for a 2.4GHz dongle once, gave me +6dB. picture looked ridiculous but it helped for streaming birds. :bird:
diego: note: check city regs if you start mounting antennas on the roof. neighbors get dramatic.
ben: quick poll: react with :rocket: if you want a step-by-step for a tinfoil dish, :seedling: if you prefer a commercial outdoor AP, :snail: if you're moving entirely to recorded meetings.
ops-bot: Reminder: please avoid posting photos that include readable customer data or internal dashboards. If you share screenshots, please blur or crop sensitive info. :lock:
matt: also pro tip — keep laptops elevated and in shade. direct sun will thermal throttle the CPU. learned that the hard way. :fire:
rachel: ran a quick iperf to the home router before and after the mini-reflector experiment:
```
Before: 9.4 Mbps down / 3.3 Mbps up / jitter 22ms
After: 14.9 Mbps down / 4.8 Mbps up / jitter 15ms
```
not enough for HD calls but better for uploads. i'll try a small UBNT outdoor AP next weekend and report.
zara: yes! and bring snacks for the roof, it's a whole production. i'll be your assistant/roof-safety-officer. :banana:
diego: if you want, i can ship you a cheap 5GHz directional panel to test. i've got one from a previous apartment hack.
ben: love the ingenuity. also, if anyone's filming rooftop content please keep the mic muted for the neighbor kids — they have opinions about your playlist. :headphones:
